question: The Vedas are considered the earliest literary record of Indo-Aryan civilisation. There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and the fourth one is _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Atharvaveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Vedas are considered the earliest literary record of Indo-Aryan civilization**__. 
 
• __**There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and the fourth one is Atharvaveda**__.
 __
 
• The** Atharva Veda** is the** "knowledge storehouse of atharvāṇas, the procedures for everyday life".**
 
• The text is the fourth Veda but has been a late addition to the Vedic scriptures of Hinduism.
 
• The language of the Atharvaveda is different from Vedic Sanskrit, preserving pre-Vedic Indo-European archaisms.
 
• It is a collection of **730 hymns with about 6,000 mantras, divided into 20 books**.
 
• About a sixth of the Atharvaveda texts adapts verses from the Rigveda, and except for Books 15 and 16, the text is mainly in verse deploying a diversity of Vedic meters.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhanurveda** is a Sanskrit treatise on warfare and archery, traditionally regarded as a upaveda attached to Yajurveda (1100 – 800 BCE) and attributed either to Bhrigu or Vishvamitra, or Bharadwaj.

 
 
• It is one among the four upavedas to Vedas (along with **Ayurveda, Gandharvaveda, and Sthapatyaveda).**
 
 
 
• **Ayurveda** is a traditional system of medicine with historical roots in the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
• It is traditionally considered the Upaveda associated with the Atharvaveda.
 
• Ayurveda focuses on the balance of body, mind, and spirit, and is widely practiced in India and Nepal.
 
 
 
• **Shilpaveda** is considered as the Upaveda instead of Arthashastra according to Charanavyuha and Katyayana.
 
 
• The Upavedas supplement the Vedas with more specific applications of Vedic teachings into the cultural field.
 
• Upavedas are considered as a part of Veda and not as a separate entity according to a few scholars, in such case there are Chaturdhasha Vidyasthanas only.
